title: Trump names intelligence chief Clayton as AI czar, to head task force, WSJ reports
source_used: The Wall Street Journal (relayed by Reuters, Scripps News and AFP via Turkiye Today)
key_facts: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton is to serve as the Trump administration's AI czar and chair a new White House task force, the Wall Street Journal reported on 3 Oct 2026; Reuters, CNBC and others relayed the report.
On 4 Oct 2026 the Journal published Clayton's description of the task force's goals: it has 120 days to deliver its findings.

The body is named the 'Super Intelligence Force', using the administration's preferred word 'superintelligence' for AI; it is to review existing law, steps Congress could take, and how breaches, hacks and model jailbreaks are reported to government.
Its charter calls for plans against AI-enabled threats 'while preventing overregulation and regulatory capture'.
Members reportedly include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
Clayton, a former SEC chairman and Wall Street lawyer confirmed as intelligence chief in July, has no technology industry background; he would be the second informal AI czar after David Sacks.
The task force follows a 29 Sep 2026 White House meeting with tech executives who, Trump said, signed a 'morally binding' agreement on AI controls.
AFP noted the appointment had not yet been formally confirmed by the White House.
quote_evidence: The “Super Intelligence Force,” chaired by Clayton, will have 120 days to prepare its findings, the Journal reported Saturday.
“The risk of not being first is high,” he added.
Clayton, the U.S. director of national intelligence, is widely reported to be the Trump administration’s new AI czar, although the appointment has not yet been confirmed.
why_it_matters_hint: The administration is putting its AI policy in the hands of its intelligence chief with a 120-day review that explicitly aims to avoid heavier regulation.
notes: Reuters page returned 401 and WSJ is paywalled; facts taken from Scripps News and from Turkiye Today's AFP text, both relaying the WSJ. Follow-up of yesterday's item 1003:C13-08 (the naming); new today: the task force's charter, members and 120-day deadline.
